subject: Reserved GPU Rollout: Implementation Playlist & Regional Capacity Decisions
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@nebula.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-team@nebula.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity inquiry — regional sizing questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited about Redwood Dedicated. I pulled together a first-pass capacity spreadsheet (attached) and a few questions we need answered quickly to lock a timeline with our procurement team: 

- Can the dedicated pool be split across two regions (us-west-2 + us-east-1) under a single reserved contract, or do we need separate reservations?
- What are typical burst policies when traffic spikes 3-5x for short windows (under 2 hours)? Do you recommend autoscaling + burst credits or a reserved baseline plus manual burst?
- What's the expected lead time to provision a G4dn-like baseline vs an H100-class pool?

We aim to start onboarding engineering in early December but procurement needs an annotated SOW and a recommended rollout plan by Nov 5. I'm attaching the workbook: nebula_capacity_requirements.xlsx.

Can you loop in the right implementation folks?

Best,
Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Platform Partnerships | Nebula AI

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@nebula.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity inquiry — regional sizing questions

Claire — thanks for the workbook and the clear timeline. Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik (implementation PM) who will drive the implementation playlist. Quick answers inline, and we'll follow up with a proposed rollout schedule and SOW draft by Nov 3.

Inline: 
- Regions: Yes — we can either place a single logical reservation that spans AZs in one region and a separate reservation for the second region. Practically, customers prefer two reservations (one per region) for predictable capacity and failure isolation. We can model a single invoice if you want consolidated billing.
- Burst policy: Recommended pattern is "Reserved baseline + autoscale burst pool." Baseline for 24/7 steady-state (e.g., 8x A100/H100-equivalent) and an autoscale pool for short spikes. We support automatic temporary burst capacity backed by a quota of burst credits; when credits exhaust we fallback to nearest compatible variant. We'll propose specific credit sizing based on your token/sec distribution.
- Lead time: G4dn-class equivalents are typically 2-3 weeks for Dedicated provisioning; H100-class baseline is 6-8 weeks depending on availability and region. We'll list options and tradeoffs in the SOW.

Next steps (we'll include these in the SOW draft):
1) Implementation playlist (kickoff, infra prep, network + KMS, pool sizing, canary, full cutover) — Karthik will own.
2) Security checklist + SOC 2 artifacts — Marissa will own fast responses.
3) Procurement-friendly SOW + DocuSign routing by Nov 3.

Karthik/Marissa — can you take ownership? Karthik, please propose a two-phase rollout that supports a smaller single-region POC in us-west-2 and a full dual-region cutover. 

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Global Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Claire Zhou <c.zhou@nebula.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity inquiry — regional sizing questions

Claire/Hannah — thanks. I've sketched an implementation playlist and attached a baseline config (reserved_pool_config_v1.yaml) and a suggested SLO matrix. High level plan: 

Phase A (POC — us-west-2, 2-week): 
- Provision baseline reserved pool: 8 x G4dn-equivalent GPUs, 2 CPU gateway nodes
- Network peering + customer VPC setup, KMS test key exchange
- Autoscale policy: scale to +4 GPUs when 5-min average qps > 75th percentile; burst credits: 48 GPU-hours/month
- Canary traffic: route 5% of production traffic for validation

Phase B (Dual-region roll, target Dec 15): 
- Provision us-east-1 pool: 6 x H100-equivalent (if you need inference at low latency we recommend H100 variants for model kernels)
- Cross-region failover policy and model replication schedule
- Full cutover and rollback playbook (DB/checkpoint sync, KV cache prewarming)

Items I need from Nebula by Nov 2: 
- Finalized steady-state TPS and 95th-percentile token/sec numbers (sheet has placeholders)
- Network CIDR ranges and preferred region for H100s
- Procurement contact for DocuSign routing

I'll convert this into a one-page timeline and an SOW appendix for Hannah and Marissa to review.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Implementation PM | Redwood Inference
Attachment: reserved_pool_config_v1.yaml (text)

From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@nebula.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-team@nebula.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity inquiry — regional sizing questions

Thanks Karthik — this looks actionable. A few clarifications from Infra: 

- We can confirm steady-state: 25 requests/sec (avg) with 95th at 120 req/sec; token/sec distribution attached in the workbook.
- Nebula would prefer consolidated billing and a single contract but two logical reservations if that keeps latency predictability.
- Procurement contact: Marcus Lee, m.lee@nebula.ai. Please route the SOW to him for signatures.

We'll review your Phase A plan internally and return the CIDR ranges by EOD Nov 2. Also attached: a draft SOW they asked us to start from (nebula_sow_draft.pdf).

Claire

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@nebula.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity inquiry — regional sizing questions

Claire — great, welcome aboard. I've added a security artifacts checklist and SOC 2 evidence bundle to the shared Drive (link below) and will start the SOW edits to include the dual-reservation billing option and burst-credit terms. Expect a redline by Nov 3 morning.

Quick notes: 
- I'll propose a burst-credit pool of 72 GPU-hours/month to start; we can tune after week 2 of Phase A.
- For the H100-class nodes we recommend a staged provisioning approach (provision in canary AZ first) — reduces lead time risk.

Shared links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nebula-onboarding

Marissa 
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
